note: Review pass 6 of the undescribed mobile-app-ui images. Sheets review_07.jpg and review_08.jpg. Written from the processed web images. Palette, dimensions and contrast are measured elsewhere.

IMG-0355.title: Code editor settings - dark panel with sliders
IMG-0355.description: A dark settings panel from a code-editor app. A short header row sits at the top, then a column of labelled rows each carrying an inline numeric value or a stepper: font size, indentation and similar. Below those, a set of segmented toggles and a slider block with a filled track and a round handle, followed by dropdown rows with small chevrons. Two buttons close the panel. It is a dense control surface and stays readable because every row is the same height, every label sits left and every value right, with a single accent reserved for the slider fill.
IMG-0355.quality: Clear capture; the row labels and values are legible.

IMG-0356.title: MyHealth - daily plan with an orange floating action
IMG-0356.description: A light health-planner screen headed 'My Health Plan'. The top block carries a row of day chips with one selected, a greeting figure and a small avatar. The body is a day plan: stacked card groups for meals, medication and activity, each row with a leading icon, a title, a time and a completion state, some rows tinted amber to mark what is due. A bright orange pill button floats above the tab bar. The screen is a good reference for a schedule that mixes content types - the cards group by activity, not by time, which keeps each list short.
IMG-0356.quality: Clear capture; the plan rows are legible.

IMG-0357.title: Wellness check-in - pale green panel with a scale
IMG-0357.description: A near-white screen with a pale green wash, showing a wellness check-in. A heading sits over a large illustration of a weighing scale drawn in loose line work, with a small hand-drawn accent beneath it. Below the illustration is a slider track with a value label and a bold dark button at the foot. The screen is mostly empty and quite tall, which is the point - the illustration and one input have the whole page, so the single question feels unhurried rather than squeezed.
IMG-0357.quality: Clear capture; the heading and slider value are legible.

IMG-0358.title: Zelt - welcome dialog over a desktop-style list
IMG-0358.description: A muted green screen showing a list with a small toolbar across the top - a leading pill, two small icon buttons and a trailing button - and a short list of rows beneath. Over the middle sits a centred white dialog headed 'Welcome to Zelt', carrying two short lines of copy, a primary green button and a secondary text link over a faint decorative glow. The dialog is the reference: a first-run message delivered as a floating card over real content, so the user sees what they are being welcomed into rather than a blank backdrop.
IMG-0358.quality: Clear capture; the dialog copy and buttons are legible.

IMG-0359.title: Empty list - drawn scale illustration as placeholder
IMG-0359.description: A tall near-white list screen with a small toolbar at the top and a single faint row at the bottom. The middle of the screen is empty except for a large, very light line drawing of a weighing scale, tilted slightly. There is no explanatory text and no call to action. Filed as a reference for illustration-as-emptiness: the drawing gives the blank area a shape and a subject without adding information or demanding an action, which suits a screen a user has simply not populated yet.
IMG-0359.quality: Clear capture; the faint illustration is visible.

IMG-0360.title: Settings - record rows with toggles and a pen accent
IMG-0360.description: A pale green settings screen headed 'Settings'. A back chevron sits top-left and a pill button top-right. The body is a short list of rows - a name field, an email field, a toggled row with a switch set to on, and a small amount row - each separated by hairlines. A large, very light line drawing of a fountain pen occupies the lower half of the screen, overlapping the empty area without obscuring any control. The playful detail is the decorative object placed in dead space, which turns a five-row settings list into something with a subject.
IMG-0360.quality: Clear capture; the row labels and toggle state are legible.

IMG-0361.title: Device pairing - 'Pair Your Account' with an illustration
IMG-0361.description: A white screen centred on a pairing step. A small heading and a two-line explanation sit at the top, followed by a large illustration of a phone and a pair of hands drawn in flat colour, and a single blue pill button reading 'Pair Now' beneath it. A tab bar closes the screen. The composition is a clean example of a one-action interstitial: heading, reason, illustration, button - in that order - with nothing else on the page and no navigation above it to suggest there is more to do.
IMG-0361.quality: Clear capture; the heading and button label are legible.

IMG-0362.title: Rajdhani Express - live train tracking on a map
IMG-0362.description: A train-tracking screen. The header gives the service name in large type with the coach and date beneath, and a small share control at the right. The main field is a map with the route drawn as a red line between two station pins, labelled boxes marking the origin and destination, and a live position marker roughly halfway. A 'Upcoming Platforms' list with a section link sits below. The screen is a strong reference for route tracking: the map carries the progress, and the header and list supply the detail without repeating the geometry.
IMG-0362.quality: Clear capture; the service name and station labels are legible.

IMG-0363.title: Banking app - four carved-glass marketing screens
IMG-0363.description: Four light phone panels from a banking app, each staged as a floating screen over a pastel gradient background - yellow, peach, lilac, mint - with heavy soft shadows giving the devices a carved-glass quality. The screens themselves are simple: a welcome back panel with a summary, a card graphic with a headline, a 'Take Control of Your Money' statement, and a savings goal panel with an action. The set is a marketing-staging study: the gradient fields and the deep drop shadows do all the mood work, and the screens stay plain.
IMG-0363.quality: Clear capture; the four panels are distinguishable.

IMG-0364.title: Finance app - add-card and transfer forms compared
IMG-0364.description: Two white finance screens side by side, both dominated by form fields. The left is a card-entry or account-details form with several labelled input rows, a couple of inline pickers and a note row; the right is a transfer form with rounded input boxes, a large amount field and a green primary button at the foot. The pair is a useful form study: both use the same label-above-field convention and the same row height, so the only differences are how many fields each task genuinely needs and where the commit button sits.
IMG-0364.quality: Clear capture; the field labels are legible.

IMG-0365.title: Brokerage - $8,500 balance with a prediction market
IMG-0365.description: Two dark screens from a brokerage product. The left carries a large balance figure at the top, a promo strip promoting a fixed-rate deposit, and a set of quick-action tiles; the right shows a prediction market with a question headline, a dark 3D globe illustration, three outcome rows each with a probability figure and a coloured indicator, and a trade button. The pair is a good example of a brokerage layout that mixes two instruments - holdings and predictions - while keeping one visual language, with colour reserved for probability rather than for decoration.
IMG-0365.quality: Clear capture; the balance and outcome percentages are legible.

IMG-0366.title: Finance trends - rose-tinted chart card with filters
IMG-0366.description: A light dashboard screen set on a pale rose gradient, headed 'Your Trends'. A row of filter chips sits under the header, each with a small icon and a label. Below that is a series of chart cards: a line chart with axis labels, a couple of smaller stat cards with sparklines, and a short insights list with figures, closing on a tab bar. The screen is a neat example of a theming trick - the same dry financial charts become approachable purely by changing the background and chip tints, with no change to the chart structure itself.
IMG-0366.quality: Clear capture; the chart cards and chip labels are legible.
